fields.security_summary: ONFI 4.1 itself provides only data-integrity primitives (Parameter Page Integrity CRC, Unique-ID complement validation) and a single coarse access-control pin (WP_n disables Program/Erase). The protocol does NOT define data-at-rest encryption, host-device authentication, or replay-protected secure regions. Higher-layer security (FDE, key management, secure-erase, ATA Security feature set) is provided by the host's NAND Flash Controller / SSD firmware on top of ONFI.

security_features.name: WP_n (Write Protect pin)
security_features.scope: entire device — disables Program and Erase
security_features.description: WP_n LOW disables all Program and Erase operations on the device; Read remains permitted. WP_n shall not transition during active Program/Erase or while Write Enable is active (Section 2.19).

security_features.name: Integrity CRC (Parameter Page)
security_features.description: 16-bit CRC at bytes 254-255; polynomial 8005h, initial 4F4Eh. Detects single-cell or burst bit errors on the parameter-page array. Not a cryptographic MAC.

security_features.name: Integrity CRC (Extended Parameter Page)
security_features.description: 16-bit CRC at bytes 0-1; same polynomial 8005h and init 4F4Eh. Coverage skips the CRC bytes themselves.

security_features.name: Parameter Page redundancy
security_features.description: Host falls back to redundant copies on Integrity CRC mismatch; defends against array bit-rot on the parameter page itself.

security_features.name: Unique ID with complement
security_features.description: 16-byte UID + 16-byte bit-wise complement repeated 16 times. Host validates UID XOR complement = all ones per copy; defends against bit errors in UID retrieval.

security_features.name: Factory Defect Mapping
security_features.description: Bad blocks marked at manufacturer's facility via non-FFh bytes in spare area; protects host from using known-bad media.

security_features.name: ECC (host-side for raw NAND; EZ NAND in-package)
security_features.description: ONFI 4.x mandates ≥ 4-bit ECC per 512 B sector. Number of bits ECC correctability reported in Parameter Page byte 112 (or Extended Parameter Page Section type 2 if > 0xFE). Common ECC: BCH (older devices) or LDPC (modern TLC/QLC).

security_features.name: Status Register FAIL bit
security_features.description: FAIL bit reports unsuccessful Program / Erase / (EZ NAND) Read / ZQ Calibration. Host can detect attempted writes against a defective block.

fields.no_base_layer_confidentiality: ONFI 4.1 does NOT specify data-at-rest encryption, host-device authentication, secure boot, or replay-protected memory. An attacker with bus access can sniff all DQ traffic plaintext, including Read / Program data and parameter page. SSD-level full-disk encryption (TCG Opal, IEEE 1667) lives above ONFI in the host controller firmware.
fields.comparison_to_sibling_emmc: eMMC adds RPMB (Replay-Protected Memory Block) with HMAC-SHA256 authentication and write counter, plus Secure Erase and Secure Trim. UFS adds Universal Flash Storage Group Security. ONFI itself has no direct RPMB equivalent — security is delegated to the SSD controller / firmware layer.
fields.secure_erase: ONFI provides Block Erase (60h/D0h) which performs an electrical erase of the block. Cryptographic erase (key destruction in an encryption layer) is a higher-layer operation. Multi-plane Block Erase (60h/D1h) accelerates bulk erase. Secure-erase claims (e.g., overwrite with random + verify) are the host's responsibility.
fields.notes: ONFI 4.1 security requirements at the simplified spec level are limited to (a) data-integrity primitives (Parameter Page CRC, UID complement, Factory Defect Map), (b) WP_n access-control pin, and (c) per-LUN FAIL reporting. Cryptographic confidentiality, authentication, secure erase, and replay protection are provided by the higher-layer SSD controller firmware (FTL + crypto stack) — not by ONFI itself.
